title: Due date: the earliest candidate wins; compliance is due on its End date
custom_preconds:
1. Sign in to the Maintenance Reminders QA build as an Owner/Admin (any user who can open Settings > Maintenance and create and edit work orders and customers).
  2. Open Settings > Maintenance, press New schedule and create a throwaway schedule 'ZZAUTOTEST Reading seed' holding one routine service per reading you will seed, named 'ZZ Seed 1', 'ZZ Seed 2' and so on, each with a Calendar trigger of Every 12 months and no canned lines. Save. (If it already exists, reuse it.)
  3. In Settings > Maintenance create a schedule 'ZZAUTOTEST Due PM' with service 'PM-M' (Distance trigger At 350,000 mileage, Calendar trigger Every 12 months) and a compliance service 'CVIP' with a 12-month term and Remind before expiry of 1 month. Save.
  4. Create unit 'ZZAUTOTEST 550' as follows: Open Customers > 'ZZAUTOTEST Fleet Co' > Assets and create unit 'ZZAUTOTEST 550' with New Asset, leaving Mileage and Engine Hours empty. On its Maintenance tab press Enroll in Schedule, choose 'ZZAUTOTEST Reading seed' and give every seed service a last service date five years ago (for example 6 Oct 2021), so each seed service reads Overdue and shows on the work order card; press Enroll. Enroll it on 'ZZAUTOTEST Due PM' too, with PM-M last done today.
  5. Readings for 'ZZAUTOTEST 550' (oldest first): 1) 11 Sep 2026 · 343,000 mileage; 2) 21 Sep 2026 · 344,000 mileage; 3) 1 Oct 2026 · 345,000 mileage. Dates are for a run on 6 Oct 2026. On another day, move every date by the same number of days and seed and read on the same day, because an estimate and a reading's age both count days up to today.
  6. Seed each reading in the table, oldest first: open Work Orders and press New Work Order for the unit; type the reading's mileage in the work order's Mileage field (and its engine hours in Engine Hours where the table gives one; leave the field untouched where it does not) and save; expand the Maintenance schedule card, open the three-dot menu of a seed service not used yet, choose Mark complete, keep On a work order with this work order chosen, set Reset date to the reading's date and press Mark complete. That work order's values become readings dated the Reset date. Confirm any warning the field shows.
  7. When every reading is in: on the unit's Maintenance tab open the 'ZZAUTOTEST Reading seed' schedule's menu, choose Remove from schedule and confirm, so the seed services add no rows. Check the Mileage card's last recorded value and date match the table's last reading.
  8. Create four more units, 'ZZAUTOTEST 551' to 'ZZAUTOTEST 554', enroll each on 'ZZAUTOTEST Due PM', and on each Maintenance tab press Add record for CVIP with Term 12 months and Start date: 551 = 26 Oct 2025 (End 26 Oct 2026, inside the month before expiry); 552 = 6 Oct 2025 (End today); 553 = 5 Oct 2025 (End yesterday); 554 = 26 Dec 2025 (End 26 Dec 2026, more than a month away).
custom_steps:
1. Open unit 550's Maintenance tab and read PM-M's Due cell and the trigger beneath it; open the row menu and read the other candidate.
  2. Work out by hand: rate (345,000 − 343,000) ÷ 20 = 100 a day; 350,000 − 345,000 = 5,000 to go = 50 days after the last reading (1 Oct 2026) = 20 Nov 2026. The calendar candidate is 6 Oct 2027.
  3. Open units 551 to 554 and read CVIP's due date and badge on each.
  4. On unit 550's Maintenance tab hover the (i) on the Due column heading and read it.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • PM-M's Due cell shows Nov 2026 from the mileage estimate, the earlier of its two candidates; the row menu lists the calendar candidate (Oct 2027).
  • 551: CVIP is due on 26 Oct 2026, its End date, and reads due soon (inside its Remind before expiry).
  • 552: CVIP is due today, its End date.
  • 553: CVIP is overdue from the day after its End date (End 5 Oct 2026).
  • 554: CVIP shows its End date, 26 Dec 2026, with no due badge yet.
  • The Due column's (i) explains the rule (in the design: “The earliest candidate and the trigger that produced it. Other candidates are in the row menu. A date known only to the month shows the month. Every estimate shows a month with its confidence; once due, the badge carries it.”).

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-3780 (Maintenance Reminders); story SV-10569 (S12, Due date resolution); Chunk 2 MR (Confluence 897679389) as edited 5 October 2026, S12; Design MR_V2_2 (Claude Design export, 6 Oct 2026), driven in full on 6 Oct 2026, Chunk 1 board artboards S4 / X1t; read 6 Oct 2026. Source-verified 6 October 2026; not yet build-verified.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S12-R5: “Due will be the earliest candidate”
  • S12-R4: “A compliance service is due on its current certificate's End date. It reads due soon from its Remind before expiry, due today on that day and overdue from the next day”
  • S12-R7: “the row menu lists every other candidate with its date and trigger”
  • S18-R19: “Mark complete On a work order also records that work order's mileage and engine hours as the asset's readings, dated the Reset date”
  • Design, Chunk 1 board, artboards S4 / X1t / M1u / M6, (i) on the Due column: “The earliest candidate and the trigger that produced it. Other candidates are in the row menu. A date known only to the month shows the month. Every estimate shows a month with its confidence; once due, the badge carries it.”
